answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a proof-of-elapsed-time lottery: each epoch, every identity's trusted enclave draws a random wait, like a falcon circling before it dives, and only the identity whose wait ends first may attest work at the summit of the epoch. The wait is real time, enforced by hardware, so one operator cannot hurry a thousand fakes past the horizon of the draw - each fake needs its own enclave actually waiting. An honest agent waits once and earns; a farm pays a thousand enclaves and a thousand waits for the same single win.
